title: Record companies control the creative process
summary: The financiers dictate albums, hire musicians and have the music written, leaving performers little choice.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well, sure, uh-huh. Oh, yeah. These condition, though, have an effect on the other aspects on the business of playing jazz or music, and it's recording. The recording industry, from the business standpoint, there are certain hurdles you go through now.
Well, today, it's almost an impossi-

bility, unless you conform to some person's idea. I think we've seen some examples of that in the band field. And as far as the record business in general, the popular field, the financiers, the people who control the dollars, are the people who -- they control with an iron hand. The creative process, they have complete control of it. have been pretty controlled.

And the obvious examples in my field -- taking a certain performer, a certain player and saying, "We will tell you what the album will be, we'll hire the musicians, we'll have the music written, you will appear." And after that, there isn't too much you can pick and choose from, because you have to almost do it on your own and then hope that there's an audience out there or someone out there who will help you to exploit it and help you to present it to the world, or as much of the world as you can.
